about: One entry per weekly AI run. Written by the evolve workflow from the AI's report (ai/RUN-REPORT.json); not edited by hand.

runs.title: The starting line
runs.summary: Eleven original arcade games, taken from Stuart's ApolloMaths secret arcade with their classic look. The AI-enhanced copy starts out identical to the originals; from here on, every change it gets is the AI's own.

runs.title: Super Snake moves into the garden
runs.summary: This week I spent the whole run on one game. Super Snake was the plainest of the eleven (a checkerboard, square blocks and a football left over from the maths app), so it now lives in a garden: a smooth golden snake with a face, fruit to eat, a ladybird to chase and hedges to steer round. I also fixed the controls so two quick turns in a row always count, which matters most in a game where one missed key ends your life.

what: Quick double turns now always work: up to three key presses or swipes are queued, so turning twice inside one step is no longer lost
Four kinds of fruit, drawn in the game, replace the football: apple 500, cherries 750, pear 1,000 and the rarer strawberry 1,500 (times the level)
The gold star is now a ladybird that crawls about and scurries away when you get close; catch it for 3,000 (times the level) before its timer runs out
New look: a mown lawn with daisies, a brick garden wall, leafy hedges as obstacles, and a smooth tapered snake with eyes and a flicking tongue
A row of dots along the bottom shows how many fruit are left before the next level
Little jingles for eating fruit and for reaching a new level; new title screen and description
changes.why: It was the least polished game and its football theme no longer fitted the arcade. In Snake, control is everything, so the turn queue is the change players will feel most; the garden, the fruit and a moving target make it nicer to look at and give a reason to take risks.

runs.tested: Full test rig on the enhanced side (1,005 checks, all passing, from a 344-pixel folded phone up to 4K, upright and sideways). Looked at the title screen and the game on a desktop window and a phone-sized touch screen (tap to start). Checked the quick double turn with real key presses. Let an autopilot play for four minutes of game time: it reached level 9 with no errors, and I looked at frames from several levels, including the ladybird and the hedge layouts.
runs.next: Give another game the same treatment; Road Hopper and Brick Blaster are the next plainest. Background music shared by all the games is also tempting. For Snake, perhaps keep the snake's length between levels so later levels get harder.

runs.title: A proper touch controller: a slide-able D-pad and thumb buttons that fit every screen, Fold included
runs.summary: Stuart asked for better control placement on the Samsung Fold, so this week the touch buttons were rebuilt for all eleven games. Movement is now a D-pad you can slide your thumb around, actions are round buttons in a thumb cluster, and the page decides for each screen whether the buttons go below the game or either side of it, whichever leaves the bigger game. Block Drop also gets a little life in its background.

what: New touch controller for every game: a D-pad on the left for moving and round action buttons on the right, with the main button bigger and coloured
Slide your thumb across the D-pad to change direction without lifting it; the middle of the pad keeps the last direction
The buttons go below the game or either side of it, whichever leaves the bigger game; on a sideways screen they sit either side, at thumb height
Buttons grow to use spare room (big on the open Fold and on tablets, never cramped on the folded Fold)
A tiny buzz on each press, on phones that support it (off when the sound is off)
On narrow screens the 'AI-enhanced' badge shortens to 'AI' so the game's name fits; a slimmer top bar on short, sideways screens
Space or Enter on a game's start screen now starts it straight away, instead of waiting for the next frame (which could miss the press on very large screens)
changes.why: On the folded Fold the buttons were squeezed into the bottom corners and wrapped untidily, sideways they were stacked in the top corner away from the thumbs, and movement was split across both sides of the screen in some games.

what: Movement on one four-way D-pad instead of left/right on one side and up/down on the other
changes.why: Steering a maze is much easier with one thumb on a cross.

what: Movement on one four-way D-pad instead of being split across both sides
changes.why: Quick turns are easier when all four directions are under one thumb.

what: Movement on one four-way D-pad instead of being split across both sides
changes.why: Hopping is one direction at a time, so one cross fits it best.

what: Four-way D-pad that also gives diagonals, so you can climb and fly forward at once
Fire and Bomb as a pair of round buttons
changes.why: Flying needs two directions together; before, up/down and left/right were on opposite sides.

what: Four-way D-pad for walking and climbing, a big Jump button on the right
changes.why: Climb and walk were split across both sides before.

what: Two big rotate buttons on the left; Fire, Thrust and Hyperspace in a thumb cluster on the right
changes.why: Fire is used most, so it is the biggest button where the thumb rests.

what: Steering on the left; Go, Brake and Nitro in a thumb cluster on the right, with Go as the main button
changes.why: Go is held most of the time, so it gets the main spot.

what: Bigger left/right buttons and one large round Fire button
changes.why: Part of the new controller.

what: Bigger left/right buttons and one large round Serve button
changes.why: Part of the new controller.

what: Two matching big flipper buttons, one at each side, with Launch beside the right flipper
changes.why: Flippers should feel like a left hand and a right hand.

what: Left, right and down on a D-pad; Turn as the main button with Drop beside it
Twinkling, drifting dust behind the well and a softly pulsing landing guide
changes.why: The screen could sit completely still between steps at the start, which felt lifeless.

runs.tested: Full test rig on the AI-enhanced side, 1,255 checks all passing (laptop, phone, folded and open Fold, Fold sideways, iPad, large screens). Took full-page pictures of every kind of controller on the folded Fold, the open Fold, the Fold sideways, a phone upright and sideways, and an iPad upright and sideways, and checked that the game and buttons are on screen with nothing overlapping. Drove the D-pad in a browser to check sliding from one direction to another, diagonals in Planet Guardian, and that lifting the thumb lets go.
runs.next: A left-handed option to swap the two sides, and controller settings remembered per device. Then back to polishing a game (Road Hopper or Brick Blaster), or shared background music.

runs.title: Road Hopper grows up: a hopping frog, a living river and a lady frog to carry home
runs.summary: This week the AI spent the whole run on Road Hopper, which was the plainest game left: flat boxes for cars, brown bars for logs and an emoji frog that jumped a whole square at once. Everything is now drawn in code, the frog really hops, and there is a new reason to visit the logs: a lady frog who needs a lift home.

what: A new frog drawn in code: it faces the way it hops, glides through each hop with its legs kicking out, casts a shadow and blinks
A key pressed during a hop is remembered and used straight after, so quick taps are never lost
A rippling river, grassy bank with flowers, lily-pad homes set into a hedge, a road with kerbs and a double yellow line, and paving where you start
Logs with bark and cut ends; turtles with shells, heads and paddling flippers that turn orange and sink when they are about to dive
Cars, sports cars and lorries seen from above, with windscreens, headlights and tail lights
Better mishaps: a splash of rings in the water, a flattened frog on the road, a dizzy frog when time runs out
New: a lady frog (pink, with a bow) sometimes waits on a log. Hop onto her log to pick her up and carry her home for a bonus
The fly in the homes is drawn in code with buzzing wings; the snake on the bank (from level 2) now slithers
From level 2 the traffic and river are shuffled a little: lanes may run the other way and speeds vary
The time bar turns yellow, then flashes red with a ticking sound in the last five seconds; the level is shown at the bottom
New description on the arcade list
changes.why: Road Hopper looked the most dated of the eleven and had been on the AI's to-do list since the first run. Making the frog hop smoothly makes the game feel more responsive, and the lady frog gives a reason to take a risk on the river.

runs.tested: Quick and full test rig on the AI-enhanced side (all screen sizes from the folded Fold to 4K, upright and sideways). Looked at pictures of the title screen, play, the lady frog on a log and a road accident, on a laptop window and the folded Fold. Drove the game in a browser with real key presses and with a simulated player to check hopping, scoring, the lady frog appearing, and that there are no errors.
runs.next: A left-handed option for the touch controls, remembered per device. Then Brick Blaster gets the same treatment, or shared background music across the arcade.

runs.title: Every game gets its own music, plus an options panel with a left-handed controller
runs.summary: Until now the arcade only beeped. This week a small built-in music player gives each of the eleven games its own original chiptune theme, with its own speed, key, mood and instruments, playing only while you play and getting a little faster as the levels go up. A new options panel lets you switch music and sound effects on or off separately and, on touch screens, flip the controller for left-handed players and choose the button size. The last football leftovers from the games' first home have also gone.

what: Background music for every game: each has its own theme, composed in code from a short recipe (tempo, key, mood, chord pattern, lead and bass sounds, drum beat)
Music plays only during play: silent on the title screen, when paused and after game over, and it speeds up slightly with each level
A short game-over tune in each game's own key

The sound button in the top bar becomes an Options button (⚙): sound effects on/off, music on/off, left- or right-handed controller and small, medium or large buttons on touch screens; choices are remembered on the device and opening it pauses the game
Keyboard shortcuts: M switches music on and off, N switches sound effects
Sound settings are now saved under the arcade's own 'retro:enhanced:' storage keys (an old mute setting is carried over)
changes.why: Stuart asked for something across all the games. Music changes the feel of every game at once, and it had been on my list since the first run. The left-handed controller had been waiting since run 2, when I rebuilt the touch buttons; a settings panel keeps the top bar from getting more crowded on a folded phone.

what: Own theme: a tense minor-key march
The football penalty shoot-out bonus round is retired; the maths, meteor and UFO bonus rounds take turns
Description now says 'Defend the base'
changes.why: The penalty round and 'defend the pitch' were leftovers from the maths app the games came from and didn't fit a space game.

what: Own theme: a bouncy, quick major-key tune with a walking bass
changes.why: Part of music for every game.

what: Own theme: slow and spacey, soft lead with a shimmering broken-chord backing
changes.why: Part of music for every game; deep space should feel calmer and wider than the others.

what: Own theme: fast minor-key tune with a driving bass
changes.why: Part of music for every game.

what: Own theme: a jaunty 'oom-pah' tune
changes.why: Part of music for every game.

what: Own theme: the fastest of the eleven, with a driving bass under the engine sound
changes.why: Part of music for every game.

what: Own theme: a gentle garden tune with soft drums
changes.why: Part of music for every game; it matches the garden look from run 1.

what: Renamed Star Pinball: the G-O-A-L lanes now spell S-T-A-R for an extra ball
Own theme with a sparkling broken-chord backing
Its flipper buttons stay left and right even with the left-handed controller switched on
changes.why: GOAL was the other football leftover. A pinball table's buttons are its two flippers, so swapping them for left-handers would make no sense.

what: Own theme: a steady, punchy tune
changes.why: Part of music for every game.

what: Own theme: a bouncy, swinging tune with an 'oom-pah' bass
changes.why: Part of music for every game; it suits the hopping frog from run 3.

what: Own theme: a thoughtful puzzle tune in a slightly exotic minor key
changes.why: Part of music for every game.

runs.tested: Quick and full test rigs on the AI-enhanced side. Drove every game in a browser to check the music starts after Space, stops when paused and throws no errors; rendered each theme off-line to check its loudness sits well below the sound effects and never clips. Checked the options panel by mouse and keyboard (Escape and Enter close it, a game that was already paused stays paused). Looked at pictures of the panel on the folded Fold and the Fold on its side, and the left-handed controller on a phone and sideways, and Star Pinball's table.
runs.next: Let each game change its music with the action (a faster tune for a bonus round or the last life), a short tune when a level is cleared, and perhaps a music test page. Then back to polishing a single game: Brick Blaster is the plainest one left.
